CrisisMMD Disaster-Damage Classification — Final Consolidated Research Notebook¶

Project: Vision Transformer (ViT), ConViT and DINOv2 for three-class disaster-image damage classification
Purpose: Consolidate the experimental journey, reported validation results, selected checkpoint and locked test-set evaluation in one auditable notebook.

Interpretation rule: This notebook distinguishes (1) the initial backbone comparison, (2) exploratory learning-rate/fine-tuning/head/loss experiments, (3) the controlled augmentation comparison, and (4) the final held-out test evaluation. Results from different experiment series are not treated as a single controlled ablation unless the setup was controlled. Reported metrics are historical results captured from the project runs; rerunning training cells can produce different values if runtime, data, package versions or randomness differ.

Executive result¶

The selected checkpoint is E07_Aug_Realistic_FocalG1 (MLflow run bc6de0c9e94a4addbf10c27936d98a4a), selected using validation Macro-F1. Its final held-out test results were Accuracy 69.41%, Balanced Accuracy 61.30%, Macro-F1 59.78%, and Weighted F1 70.23% on 693 test images. This is a measured baseline for research—not a claim of deployment readiness or near-perfect performance.

The class-wise supports printed in the final classification report do not align with the expected stratified split order (the report shows supports 95, 165, 433 for little/no, mild and severe respectively, while the inventory suggests approximately 433, 165, 95 in that order). Therefore, verify the dataset class-to-index mapping and the order passed to classification_report before making class-specific claims. The aggregate test metrics are reported as captured; class-level interpretation is provisional until this mapping is confirmed.

2. Consolidated results — all major experiment stages¶

2.1 Initial frozen linear-probe comparison¶

Backbone / experiment Validation accuracy Validation balanced accuracy Validation Macro-F1 Interpretation
ViT Base (vit_base_patch16_224.augreg_in21k_ft_in1k) 58.15% 53.36% 51.57% Standard pretrained ViT baseline
ConViT Tiny (convit_tiny.fb_in1k) 58.87% 51.12% 50.02% Lightweight convolutional-inductive-bias baseline
DINOv2 Base (vit_base_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m) 62.77% 59.30% 57.30% Strongest initial frozen representation

The first comparison supports using DINOv2 as the main candidate for further investigation. It does not prove that DINOv2 is universally superior: the models differ in pretraining, architecture and parameterization.

2.2 DINOv2 learning-rate and fine-tuning exploration¶

Experiment Validation accuracy Balanced accuracy Macro-F1 Notes
Initial frozen DINOv2 probe 62.77% 59.30% 57.30% Starting point
Learning-rate sweep: best reported LR = 3e-4 65.95% 60.92% 59.10% Best among tested learning rates 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3
Partial fine-tuning, one block 66.96% 62.09% 60.00% Validation Macro-F1 improved over frozen probe
Partial fine-tuning, two blocks 68.40% 61.47% 59.47% Higher accuracy did not translate into higher Macro-F1

The learning-rate and unfreezing trials indicate that adapting pretrained features can help, but the ranking depends on the metric. Accuracy favours the two-block run in this comparison, while Macro-F1 favours the one-block run. This is why the study uses Macro-F1 as the principal model-selection metric for an imbalanced three-class problem.

2.3 Classifier-head and loss experiments (separate exploratory runs)¶

Experiment Validation accuracy Balanced accuracy Macro-F1
Conv + GroupNorm head, two blocks, weighted CE + scheduler 73.88% 65.72% 64.92%
MLP head, two blocks 71.43% 65.28% 64.81%
Focal loss, gamma = 1 72.29% 64.99% 65.74%
Focal loss, gamma = 2 72.44% 63.39% 64.13%
Focal loss, gamma = 2 + label smoothing 71.57% 64.17% 63.79%

These results are from separate configurations/runs and must not be interpreted as a clean one-variable-at-a-time sequence. They suggest that head design and loss reweighting can materially affect the trade-off between aggregate accuracy and minority-class-sensitive metrics. Focal loss with gamma 1 reported the highest Macro-F1 among this particular set, whereas the Conv + GroupNorm / weighted-CE configuration reported higher accuracy and balanced accuracy. The final selected augmentation checkpoint is a later experiment with its own fixed configuration and should be judged by its own validation and test results.

2.4 Controlled augmentation comparison (same focal-loss gamma = 1 experiment family)¶

Run Augmentation Best epoch Validation accuracy Balanced accuracy Macro-F1 Recorded training time
E07_Aug_Baseline_FocalG1 Baseline 6 72.73% 63.32% 64.07% 422.57 s
E07_Aug_Realistic_FocalG1 Realistic 5 71.72% 65.60% 64.18% 449.48 s
E07_Aug_RandAugment_FocalG1 RandAugment 3 68.98% 66.38% 63.53% 286.86 s

Decision: Realistic augmentation was selected because it produced the highest validation Macro-F1 in this controlled augmentation series, although the margin over baseline was small (+0.11 percentage points). RandAugment had the highest balanced accuracy and shortest recorded training time, but lower Macro-F1 and accuracy. Timing values are specific to these recorded runs and are not a hardware-independent benchmark. The decision reflects a metric-led trade-off, not an assertion that realistic augmentation wins on every metric.

Important validation check: The supports above are copied from the recorded output and are inconsistent with the stated inventory order under a conventional stratified 80/20 split. Do not present the apparent class-wise ranking as definitive until class_to_idx, target encoding, prediction decoding and target_names ordering are checked. This notebook deliberately preserves the observed output rather than silently changing labels or inventing corrected per-class scores.

4. What the results mean¶

  1. Pretrained representation matters. DINOv2 had the strongest initial frozen-probe Macro-F1 among the three backbones evaluated.
  2. Fine-tuning is not monotonic. Unfreezing more layers and raising accuracy did not always improve Macro-F1, demonstrating that a single headline metric can obscure class-level trade-offs.
  3. The augmentation decision was evidence-led. Realistic augmentation had a small Macro-F1 advantage; RandAugment traded some Macro-F1/accuracy for higher balanced accuracy and lower observed runtime.
  4. Generalization remains limited. The selected model's validation Macro-F1 (64.18%) exceeded test Macro-F1 (59.78%) by 4.40 percentage points. The corresponding balanced-accuracy gap was 4.30 points. This may reflect sampling variability, distribution differences or overfitting to validation; the test set must not be reused for tuning.
  5. No deployment claim is warranted. Disaster-damage classification is safety-relevant. Model predictions should be treated as decision support and validated across unseen disaster events, regions, devices, image conditions and class distributions before operational use.

5. Reproducibility and notebook execution¶

The detailed code and captured experiment outputs from the source notebook are retained below in research order. The notebook includes environment setup, data and annotation audit, image integrity checks, split creation, backbone baselines, DINOv2 fine-tuning, head/loss experiments, augmentation trials and final test evaluation. In Databricks, confirm that DATASET_ROOT, MLflow access and checkpoint paths point to the intended data and runs before executing cells. Some cells are environment-specific and may need to be run in order.

Final protocol: select models using validation data only; load the selected checkpoint once; evaluate on the held-out test split; report all relevant metrics; audit label ordering; and reserve event-held-out testing for a stronger generalization study.

1. Experiment plan¶

Family Candidate Purpose
Standard ViT ImageNet-pretrained ViT-Base/16 Transformer baseline
ConViT Pretrained ConViT-Tiny Tests convolutional inductive bias combined with attention
Advanced representation DINOv2 ViT-Base Tests a strong self-supervised visual representation

Each architecture will be tested with a small, configurable search over learning rate, weight decay and backbone freezing. To keep the first run manageable, start with 2 trials per model and a small smoke-test subset. Increase the search only after the pipeline works end-to-end.

Research question: Which pretrained visual architecture and fine-tuning configuration offers the best trade-off between macro-F1, rare-class recall, training cost and inference latency on the chosen crisis-image labels?

2. Dataset loading and annotation audit¶

Load CrisisMMD annotation TSV files and resolve image paths. Audit missing paths, unreadable images, dimensions, exact SHA-256 duplicates, and label coverage before model training. Only rows with usable image_damage labels can enter the supervised task; the full annotation row count is not the same as the labeled training population.

import os
import glob
import pandas as pd

DATASET_ROOT = (
    "/Workspace/Users/hmk797@uowmail.edu.au/"
    "Deep Learning 901 Work Stream/VIT Research Project/"
    "CrisisMMD_v2.0"
)

ANNOTATIONS_DIR = os.path.join(DATASET_ROOT, "annotations")
IMAGE_ROOT = os.path.join(DATASET_ROOT, "data_image")

tsv_files = sorted(
    path for path in glob.glob(
        os.path.join(ANNOTATIONS_DIR, "*.tsv")
    )
    if not os.path.basename(path).startswith("._")
)

print("Annotation TSV files found:", len(tsv_files))

frames = []

for path in tsv_files:
    temp = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", dtype=str)
    temp["annotation_file"] = os.path.basename(path)
    temp["event_id"] = os.path.basename(path).replace(
        "_final_data.tsv", ""
    )
    frames.append(temp)

if not frames:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"No annotation TSV files found in {ANNOTATIONS_DIR}"
    )

df = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

print("\nTotal annotation rows:", len(df))
print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())
print("\nRows by annotation file:")
print(df["annotation_file"].value_counts().to_string())

print("\nSample annotation records:")
display(df.head(5))

import os
import pandas as pd
from tqdm.auto import tqdm

DATASET_ROOT = (
    "/Workspace/Users/hmk797@uowmail.edu.au/"
    "Deep Learning 901 Work Stream/VIT Research Project/"
    "CrisisMMD_v2.0"
)

# Fail early if the annotation DataFrame is missing or has an unexpected schema.
if "df" not in globals():
    raise NameError(
        "DataFrame 'df' is not defined. Run the annotation-loading cell first."
    )

if "image_path" not in df.columns:
    raise ValueError(
        f"Missing 'image_path' column. Available columns: {df.columns.tolist()}"
    )

# Resolve annotation paths and check whether the files exist.
df["resolved_path"] = df["image_path"].apply(
    lambda p: os.path.normpath(os.path.join(DATASET_ROOT, str(p)))
    if pd.notna(p) and str(p).strip()
    else None
)

df["path_exists"] = df["resolved_path"].apply(
    lambda p: os.path.isfile(p) if p else False
)

total = len(df)
found = int(df["path_exists"].sum())
missing = total - found

print("=" * 55)
print("IMAGE PATH MATCHING RESULTS")
print("=" * 55)
print("Annotation rows:", total)
print("Paths found:", found)
print("Paths missing:", missing)
print(
    "Path match rate:",
    f"{found / total * 100:.2f}%" if total else "N/A (empty dataset)"
)

print("\nExamples of resolved paths:")
display(df[["image_path", "resolved_path", "path_exists"]].head(10))

print("\nMissing path examples:")
missing_df = df.loc[
    ~df["path_exists"], ["image_path", "resolved_path"]
]
if missing_df.empty:
    print("No missing image paths.")
else:
    display(missing_df.head(10))

import os
import hashlib
import pandas as pd
from PIL import Image
from tqdm.auto import tqdm

valid_records = []
audit_errors = []

for row in tqdm(
    df.itertuples(index=False),
    total=len(df),
    desc="Auditing CrisisMMD images"
):
    path = row.resolved_path

    try:
        with Image.open(path) as img:
            img.verify()

        with Image.open(path) as img:
            width, height = img.size
            mode = img.mode

        sha256 = hashlib.sha256()

        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                sha256.update(chunk)

        valid_records.append({
            "image_path": row.image_path,
            "resolved_path": path,
            "sha256": sha256.hexdigest(),
            "width": width,
            "height": height,
            "mode": mode,
        })

    except Exception as exc:
        audit_errors.append({
            "image_path": row.image_path,
            "resolved_path": path,
            "error": str(exc),
        })

audit_df = pd.DataFrame(valid_records)
errors_df = pd.DataFrame(audit_errors)

unique_hashes = (
    audit_df["sha256"].nunique()
    if not audit_df.empty else 0
)

print("\n" + "=" * 55)
print("CRISIS MMD IMAGE AUDIT")
print("=" * 55)
print(f"Annotation rows:           {len(df):,}")
print(f"Existing image paths:      {df['path_exists'].sum():,}")
print(f"Valid images:              {len(audit_df):,}")
print(f"Unreadable images:         {len(errors_df):,}")
print(f"Unique exact image hashes: {unique_hashes:,}")
print(f"Duplicate image rows:      {len(audit_df) - unique_hashes:,}")

if not audit_df.empty:
    print("\nMost common image dimensions:")
    display(
        audit_df.groupby(["width", "height", "mode"])
        .size()
        .reset_index(name="count")
        .sort_values("count", ascending=False)
        .head(15)
    )

if not errors_df.empty:
    print("\nFirst 10 image errors:")
    display(errors_df.head(10))

import pandas as pd

# Recalculate duplicate statistics
n_rows = len(audit_df)
n_unique = audit_df["sha256"].nunique()

print("Audit rows:", n_rows)
print("Unique exact image hashes:", n_unique)
print("Duplicate rows:", n_rows - n_unique)

# Join image hashes to the original annotations
audit_labels = audit_df[
    ["image_path", "sha256"]
].merge(
    df[["image_path", "image_damage", "event_id"]],
    on="image_path",
    how="left",
    validate="one_to_one"
)

print("\nRows after joining labels:", len(audit_labels))
print("Missing image_damage labels:", audit_labels["image_damage"].isna().sum())

# Inspect duplicate groups
duplicates = audit_labels[
    audit_labels.duplicated("sha256", keep=False)
].copy()

print("Rows in duplicate groups:", len(duplicates))
print("Duplicate hash groups:", duplicates["sha256"].nunique())

if not duplicates.empty:
    group_stats = duplicates.groupby("sha256").agg(
        rows=("sha256", "size"),
        label_count=("image_damage", "nunique"),
        event_count=("event_id", "nunique"),
        labels=("image_damage", lambda x: sorted(x.dropna().unique().tolist())),
    ).reset_index()

    print(
        "Duplicate groups with conflicting labels:",
        int((group_stats["label_count"] > 1).sum())
    )
    print(
        "Duplicate groups spanning multiple events:",
        int((group_stats["event_count"] > 1).sum())
    )

    display(
        group_stats.sort_values("rows", ascending=False).head(15)
    )

# Target class distribution
print("\nimage_damage class distribution:")
display(
    df["image_damage"]
    .fillna("MISSING")
    .value_counts(dropna=False)
    .rename_axis("image_damage")
    .reset_index(name="count")
)

import pandas as pd

TARGET_COL = "image_damage"

CLASS_NAMES = [
    "little_or_no_damage",
    "mild_damage",
    "severe_damage",
]

required_audit_cols = {"image_path", "sha256"}
required_df_cols = {"image_path", TARGET_COL}

if not required_audit_cols.issubset(audit_df.columns):
    raise ValueError(
        f"audit_df is missing columns: "
        f"{required_audit_cols - set(audit_df.columns)}"
    )

if not required_df_cols.issubset(df.columns):
    raise ValueError(
        f"df is missing columns: {required_df_cols - set(df.columns)}"
    )

# One hash per image path
hash_lookup = (
    audit_df[["image_path", "sha256"]]
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["image_path"])
)

# Start with labeled examples only
labeled = df.loc[df[TARGET_COL].isin(CLASS_NAMES)].copy()

# Remove any pre-existing hash column to avoid merge suffixes
if "sha256" in labeled.columns:
    labeled = labeled.drop(columns=["sha256"])

labeled = labeled.merge(
    hash_lookup,
    on="image_path",
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one",
)

print("Labeled rows:", len(labeled))
print("Missing hashes:", labeled["sha256"].isna().sum())
print("Unique image hashes:", labeled["sha256"].nunique())

assert labeled["sha256"].notna().all(), (
    "Some labeled images could not be matched to their audited hashes."
)

Dataset and label audit¶

This step inspects the CrisisMMD annotations and label availability before modelling. Use the observed counts to justify filtering and avoid assuming every annotation has a usable damage label.

import pandas as pd

class_order = [
    "dont_know_or_cant_judge",
    "little_or_no_damage",
    "mild_damage",
    "severe_damage",
]

# Reuse the labeled dataset if available; otherwise derive it from df.
if "labeled_df" in globals():
    source_df = labeled_df
elif "df" in globals():
    source_df = df
else:
    raise NameError(
        "Neither 'labeled_df' nor 'df' exists. Run the dataset-loading cell first."
    )

required_columns = {"event_id", "image_damage"}
missing_columns = required_columns - set(source_df.columns)

if missing_columns:
    raise ValueError(
        f"Missing required columns: {sorted(missing_columns)}"
    )

# Exclude rows without an event or damage label for this cross-tabulation.
labeled_df = source_df.dropna(
    subset=["event_id", "image_damage"]
).copy()

# Count each damage class per event, retaining classes with zero observations.
event_class_counts = pd.crosstab(
    labeled_df["event_id"],
    labeled_df["image_damage"]
).reindex(columns=class_order, fill_value=0)

print("Labeled rows:", len(labeled_df))
print("Events:", labeled_df["event_id"].nunique())

display(event_class_counts)

three_class_columns = [
    "little_or_no_damage",
    "mild_damage",

# Research step: Visually inspect sample images and their labels
import os
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from PIL import Image
import pandas as pd

# Use the cleaned dataset when available; otherwise use the loaded annotations.
if "labeled_df" in globals():
    image_df = labeled_df.copy()
elif "df" in globals():
    image_df = df.copy()
else:
    raise NameError("Run the dataset-loading cell first.")

required_cols = {"image_path", "image_damage"}
missing_cols = required_cols - set(image_df.columns)
if missing_cols:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing columns: {sorted(missing_cols)}")

# Resolve paths if an earlier cell has not already done so.
if "resolved_path" not in image_df.columns:
    DATASET_ROOT = (
        "/Workspace/Users/hmk797@uowmail.edu.au/"
        "Deep Learning 901 Work Stream/VIT Research Project/"
        "CrisisMMD_v2.0"
    )
    image_df["resolved_path"] = image_df["image_path"].apply(
        lambda p: os.path.normpath(os.path.join(DATASET_ROOT, str(p)))
        if pd.notna(p) and str(p).strip()
        else None
    )

image_df = image_df[
    image_df["resolved_path"].notna()
    & image_df["image_damage"].notna()
    & image_df["resolved_path"].apply(os.path.isfile)
].copy()

if image_df.empty:
    raise ValueError(
        "No labeled images were found at the resolved paths. "
        "Check DATASET_ROOT and the image_path values."
    )

# Sample across damage classes where possible.
sample_size = min(9, len(image_df))
class_groups = [
    group.sample(n=1, random_state=42)
    for _, group in image_df.groupby("image_damage")
    if not group.empty
]
sample_df = pd.concat(class_groups).drop_duplicates()

if len(sample_df) < sample_size:
    remaining = image_df.drop(index=sample_df.index, errors="ignore")
    extra = remaining.sample(
        n=min(sample_size - len(sample_df), len(remaining)),
        random_state=42,
    )
    sample_df = pd.concat([sample_df, extra])

sample_df = sample_df.sample(
    n=min(sample_size, len(sample_df)), random_state=42
).reset_index(drop=True)

cols = 3
rows = (len(sample_df) + cols - 1) // cols
fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(15, 5 * rows))
axes = [axes] if len(sample_df) == 1 else list(axes.flatten())

for ax, (_, row) in zip(axes, sample_df.iterrows()):
    try:
        with Image.open(row["resolved_path"]) as img:
            ax.imshow(img.convert("RGB"))
        event = row.get("event_id", "Unknown")
        ax.set_title(
            f"Label: {row['image_damage']}\nEvent: {event}",
            fontsize=10,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        ax.text(0.5, 0.5, f"Could not load image\n{exc}",
                ha="center", va="center", wrap=True)
    ax.axis("off")

for ax in axes[len(sample_df):]:
    ax.axis("off")

plt.suptitle("CrisisMMD: Sample Images by Damage Label", fontsize=15)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Image integrity and duplicate audit¶

Exact-image hashes are used to identify duplicate files and check whether duplicate images carry conflicting labels. This is a data-quality check, not a model-performance result.

In [0]:
# Find image hashes with conflicting labels
labels_per_hash = labeled.groupby("sha256")[TARGET_COL].nunique()

conflicting_hashes = labels_per_hash[
    labels_per_hash > 1
].index

print("Conflicting image groups:", len(conflicting_hashes))

# Exclude ambiguous duplicate groups
clean = labeled.loc[
    ~labeled["sha256"].isin(conflicting_hashes)
].copy()

# Keep one row per unique image
clean = clean.drop_duplicates(
    subset="sha256"
).reset_index(drop=True)

print("Clean unique labeled images:", len(clean))
print("\nClass distribution:")
display(clean[TARGET_COL].value_counts().to_frame("count"))

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

TARGET_COL = "image_damage"

CLASS_NAMES = [
    "little_or_no_damage",
    "mild_damage",
    "severe_damage",
]

# Confirm required columns
assert "image_path" in df.columns
assert TARGET_COL in df.columns
assert {"image_path", "sha256"}.issubset(audit_df.columns)

# Build a reliable image-path-to-hash lookup
hash_lookup = (
    audit_df[["image_path", "sha256"]]
    .dropna(subset=["image_path", "sha256"])
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["image_path"])
)

# Start from original annotations, not a previously filtered DataFrame
labeled = df.loc[df[TARGET_COL].isin(CLASS_NAMES)].copy()

# Remove any old hash column before merging
labeled = labeled.drop(
    columns=["sha256"],
    errors="ignore"
)

labeled = labeled.merge(
    hash_lookup,
    on="image_path",
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one"
)

assert labeled["sha256"].notna().all(), (
    "Some labeled image paths have no matching audited hash."
)

# Identify exact image content assigned multiple target labels
labels_per_hash = labeled.groupby("sha256")[TARGET_COL].nunique()
conflicting_hashes = labels_per_hash[labels_per_hash > 1].index

print("Original labeled rows:", len(labeled))
print("Conflicting image groups:", len(conflicting_hashes))
print(
    "Rows excluded due to conflicting labels:",
    labeled["sha256"].isin(conflicting_hashes).sum()
)

# Exclude ambiguous groups and retain one row per exact image
clean = labeled.loc[
    ~labeled["sha256"].isin(conflicting_hashes)
].copy()

clean = clean.drop_duplicates(
    subset="sha256"
).reset_index(drop=True)

print("\nClean unique images:", len(clean))
print("\nClass distribution:")
display(clean[TARGET_COL].value_counts().to_frame("count"))

assert clean["sha256"].is_unique
assert clean[TARGET_COL].nunique() == 3

3. Clean labels and create leakage-aware splits¶

Exclude unusable labels and conflicting duplicate groups, deduplicate exact image content, and preserve class counts. Create train/validation/test partitions once, then persist the split manifests. The source notebook uses a stratified random split; it does not establish event-held-out generalization, so that limitation must remain explicit in the report.

4. Train/validation/test split¶

Preferred strategy: hold out entire event IDs for test, when there are enough valid events. Otherwise use a stratified random split and clearly label it as a weaker evaluation. A random split does not establish generalization to unseen disasters.

Shared imports and runtime checks¶

Imports and runtime checks belong in the setup stage. Later cells should reuse these names rather than re-importing libraries or reinstalling packages.

In [0]:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

SEED = 42

trainval_df, test_df = train_test_split(
    clean,
    test_size=0.20,
    random_state=SEED,
    stratify=clean[TARGET_COL],
)

train_df, val_df = train_test_split(
    trainval_df,
    test_size=0.25,
    random_state=SEED,
    stratify=trainval_df[TARGET_COL],
)

# Check exact-image leakage
train_hashes = set(train_df["sha256"])
val_hashes = set(val_df["sha256"])
test_hashes = set(test_df["sha256"])

assert train_hashes.isdisjoint(val_hashes)
assert train_hashes.isdisjoint(test_hashes)
assert val_hashes.isdisjoint(test_hashes)

print("Train:", len(train_df))
print("Validation:", len(val_df))
print("Test:", len(test_df))

print("\nClass counts per split:")
display(pd.DataFrame({
    "train": train_df[TARGET_COL].value_counts(),
    "validation": val_df[TARGET_COL].value_counts(),
    "test": test_df[TARGET_COL].value_counts(),
}).fillna(0).astype(int))

4. Baseline models: ViT first, then ConViT, then DINOv2¶

The first experiment establishes a consistent frozen-backbone/linear-probe comparison across ViT-Base, ConViT-Tiny, and DINOv2-Base. Use the same split and metric definitions. Input resolution follows each pretrained model's configuration, so this comparison is a practical baseline rather than a perfectly compute-matched architecture benchmark.

Shared imports and runtime checks¶

Imports and runtime checks belong in the setup stage. Later cells should reuse these names rather than re-importing libraries or reinstalling packages.

In [0]:
import torch
import timm
import gc

DEVICE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
NUM_CLASSES = 3

MODEL_CONFIGS = {
    "ViT_Base": "vit_base_patch16_224.augreg_in21k_ft_in1k",
    "ConViT_Tiny": "convit_tiny.fb_in1k",
    "DINOv2_Base": "vit_base_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m",
}

for model_key, model_name in MODEL_CONFIGS.items():
    print(f"\nTesting {model_key}: {model_name}")

    model = timm.create_model(
        model_name,
        pretrained=True,
        num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    ).to(DEVICE)

    model.eval()

    try:
        data_config = timm.data.resolve_model_data_config(model)
        input_h, input_w = data_config["input_size"][1:]

        print("Configured input:", (input_h, input_w))

        with torch.inference_mode():
            dummy = torch.randn(
                2, 3, input_h, input_w, device=DEVICE
            )
            output = model(dummy)

        print("Output shape:", tuple(output.shape))
        print("Data config:", data_config)

        assert output.shape == (2, NUM_CLASSES)

    finally:
        del model
        gc.collect()
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()

print("\nAll model smoke tests completed.")

Controlled classifier-head comparison¶

Compare classifier heads while holding the dataset split and backbone strategy constant. The goal is to test whether head capacity or inductive bias improves minority-class recognition, not simply to maximize accuracy.

Progressive DINOv2 fine-tuning¶

This experiment unfreezes a limited number of final backbone blocks to adapt pretrained features to disaster imagery. Compare it with the frozen linear probe, while noting that additional trainable parameters increase compute and overfitting risk.

In [0]:
model = timm.create_model(
    MODEL_CONFIGS["DINOv2_Base"],
    pretrained=True,
    num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
).to(DEVICE)

# Freeze everything first.
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False

# Unfreeze final transformer blocks.
for block in model.blocks[-2:]:
    for param in block.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True

# Unfreeze final normalization layer, if present.
if hasattr(model, "norm"):
    for param in model.norm.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True

# Unfreeze classifier.
for param in model.get_classifier().parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True

import timm
from timm.data import create_transform, resolve_model_data_config

def make_transforms(model_name, training=False):
    """Create model-compatible preprocessing for training or evaluation."""
    model = timm.create_model(
        model_name,
        pretrained=False,
        num_classes=0,
    )
    data_config = resolve_model_data_config(model)

    if training:
        transform = create_transform(
            **data_config,
            is_training=True,
        )
    else:
        transform = create_transform(
            **data_config,
            is_training=False,
        )

    del model
    return transform

from PIL import Image
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
import os
import torch

class CrisisMMDImageDataset(Dataset):
    """Load CrisisMMD images and their encoded damage labels."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        dataframe,
        transform=None,
        path_col="resolved_path",
        label_col="image_damage",
    ):
        self.df = dataframe.reset_index(drop=True).copy()
        self.transform = transform
        self.path_col = path_col
        self.label_col = label_col

        required = {path_col, label_col}
        missing = required - set(self.df.columns)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Dataset is missing columns: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        self.df = self.df.dropna(
            subset=[path_col, label_col]
        ).reset_index(drop=True)

        # Use one consistent mapping across every model and data split.
        self.class_to_idx = {
            "little_or_no_damage": 0,
            "mild_damage": 1,
            "severe_damage": 2,
        }

        self.df = self.df[
            self.df[label_col].isin(self.class_to_idx)
        ].reset_index(drop=True)

        missing_files = [
            p for p in self.df[path_col]
            if not os.path.isfile(str(p))
        ]
        if missing_files:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"{len(missing_files)} image files are missing. "
                f"Example: {missing_files[0]}"
            )

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.df)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        row = self.df.iloc[index]
        image_path = str(row[self.path_col])
        label = self.class_to_idx[row[self.label_col]]

        with Image.open(image_path) as img:
            image = img.convert("RGB")

        if self.transform is not None:
            image = self.transform(image)

        return image, torch.tensor(label, dtype=torch.long)

    eval_transform = make_transforms(model_name, training=False)

    datasets = {
        "train": CrisisMMDImageDataset(train_df, train_transform),
        "validation": CrisisMMDImageDataset(val_df, eval_transform),
        "test": CrisisMMDImageDataset(test_df, eval_transform),
    }

    try:
        for split_name, dataset in datasets.items():
            print(f"\n{split_name}: {len(dataset)} images")

            if len(dataset) == 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{split_name} dataset is empty for {model_key}."
                )

            loader = DataLoader(
                dataset,

                shuffle=(split_name == "train"),

            images, labels = next(iter(loader))

            print("Image batch:", tuple(images.shape))
            print("Label batch:", tuple(labels.shape))
            print("Label IDs present:", torch.unique(labels).tolist())

            del loader

# Original training pipeline dependencies and configuration
import os
import gc
import json
import time
import random
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import timm
import mlflow
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from sklearn.metrics import (
    f1_score,
    balanced_accuracy_score,
    accuracy_score,
    classification_report,
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay,
)

SEED = 42
NUM_CLASSES = 3
BATCH_SIZE = 16
NUM_WORKERS = 2
MAX_EPOCHS = 10
PATIENCE = 3
LEARNING_RATE = 1e-3
WEIGHT_DECAY = 1e-4

DEVICE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
EXPERIMENT_NAME = "/Shared/disaster-response-vlm-architecture-comparison"
ARTIFACT_DIR = "/tmp/crisismmd_experiment_a"
os.makedirs(ARTIFACT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
mlflow.set_experiment(EXPERIMENT_NAME)

CLASS_NAMES = [
    "little_or_no_damage",
    "mild_damage",
    "severe_damage",
]

MODEL_CONFIGS = {
    "ViT_Base": "vit_base_patch16_224.augreg_in21k_ft_in1k",
    "ConViT_Tiny": "convit_tiny.fb_in1k",
    "DINOv2_Base": "vit_base_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m",
}

def seed_everything(seed=42):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)

def evaluate_model(model, loader, criterion):
    model.eval()
    total_loss = 0.0
    y_true, y_pred = [], []

    with torch.inference_mode():
        for images, labels in loader:
            images = images.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)
            labels = labels.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)

            with torch.autocast(
                device_type="cuda",
                dtype=torch.float16,
                enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
            ):
                logits = model(images)
                loss = criterion(logits, labels)

            total_loss += loss.item() * labels.size(0)
            y_true.extend(labels.cpu().numpy())
            y_pred.extend(logits.argmax(dim=1).cpu().numpy())

    if not y_true:
        raise ValueError("Evaluation loader produced no samples.")

    return {
        "loss": total_loss / len(loader.dataset),
        "macro_f1": f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro", zero_division=0),
        "balanced_accuracy": balanced_accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred),
        "accuracy": accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred),
        "y_true": np.asarray(y_true),
        "y_pred": np.asarray(y_pred),
    }

print("Configuration and evaluation helpers defined.")

def train_linear_probe(model_key, model_name):
    seed_everything(SEED)
    start_time = time.time()

    print(f"\n{'=' * 65}\nTraining {model_key}\n{'=' * 65}")

    train_transform = make_transforms(model_name, training=True)
    eval_transform = make_transforms(model_name, training=False)

    train_dataset = CrisisMMDImageDataset(train_df, train_transform)
    val_dataset = CrisisMMDImageDataset(val_df, eval_transform)

    train_loader = DataLoader(
        train_dataset,
        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
        shuffle=True,
        num_workers=NUM_WORKERS,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
        generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(SEED),
    )
    val_loader = DataLoader(
        val_dataset,
        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
        shuffle=False,
        num_workers=NUM_WORKERS,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
    )

    model = timm.create_model(
        model_name,
        pretrained=True,
        num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    ).to(DEVICE)

    # Freeze the backbone and train only the classifier.
    for param in model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = False

    classifier = model.get_classifier()
    if not isinstance(classifier, nn.Module):
        raise TypeError(
            f"Unexpected classifier returned by {model_name}: "
            f"{type(classifier)}"
        )

    for param in classifier.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True

    trainable_params = [
        p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad
    ]
    trainable_count = sum(p.numel() for p in trainable_params)
    total_count = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())

    # Compute class weights from the training partition only.
    counts = (
        train_df["image_damage"]
        .value_counts()
        .reindex(CLASS_NAMES, fill_value=0)
    )

    if (counts == 0).any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"At least one training class has no examples: "
            f"{counts.to_dict()}"
        )

    weights = len(train_df) / (NUM_CLASSES * counts)
    class_weights = torch.tensor(
        weights.values,
        dtype=torch.float32,
        device=DEVICE,
    )

    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=class_weights)

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, model.parameters()),
        lr=1e-3,
        weight_decay=1e-4,
    )

    scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler(
        "cuda",
        enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
    )

    best_val_f1 = -1.0
    best_epoch = 0
    epochs_without_improvement = 0
    history = []

    checkpoint_path = os.path.join(
        ARTIFACT_DIR,
        f"{model_key}_best.pt",
    )

    with mlflow.start_run(
        run_name=f"{model_key}_linear_probe"
    ) as run:

        mlflow.log_params({
            "model_key": model_key,
            "model_name": model_name,
            "training_method": "frozen_backbone_linear_probe",
            "seed": SEED,
            "input_size": str(
                timm.data.resolve_model_data_config(model)["input_size"]
            ),
            "batch_size": BATCH_SIZE,
            "learning_rate": LEARNING_RATE,
            "weight_decay": WEIGHT_DECAY,
            "max_epochs": MAX_EPOCHS,
            "patience": PATIENCE,
            "optimizer": "AdamW",
            "loss": "class_weighted_cross_entropy",
            "class_names": json.dumps(CLASS_NAMES),
            "train_rows": len(train_df),
            "validation_rows": len(val_df),
            "trainable_parameters": trainable_count,
            "total_parameters": total_count,
            "device": DEVICE,
        })

        mlflow.log_metrics({
            f"train_class_count_{label}": int(counts[label])
            for label in CLASS_NAMES
        })

        for epoch in range(1, MAX_EPOCHS + 1):
            # Keep the frozen backbone in evaluation mode.
            model.eval()
            model.get_classifier().train()

            running_loss = 0.0

            for images, labels in train_loader:
                images = images.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)
                labels = labels.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)

                optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)

                with torch.autocast(
                    device_type="cuda",
                    dtype=torch.float16,
                    enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
                ):
                    logits = model(images)
                    loss = criterion(logits, labels)

                scaler.scale(loss).backward()
                scaler.step(optimizer)
                scaler.update()

                running_loss += loss.item() * labels.size(0)

            train_loss = running_loss / len(train_dataset)
            val_metrics = evaluate_model(
                model, val_loader, criterion
            )

            record = {
                "epoch": epoch,
                "train_loss": train_loss,
                "val_loss": val_metrics["loss"],
                "val_macro_f1": val_metrics["macro_f1"],
                "val_balanced_accuracy": val_metrics[
                    "balanced_accuracy"
                ],
                "val_accuracy": val_metrics["accuracy"],
            }
            history.append(record)

            mlflow.log_metrics(
                {
                    key: float(value)
                    for key, value in record.items()
                    if key != "epoch"
                },
                step=epoch,
            )

            print(
                f"Epoch {epoch:02d}/{MAX_EPOCHS} | "
                f"train_loss={train_loss:.4f} | "
                f"val_loss={val_metrics['loss']:.4f} | "
                f"val_macro_f1={val_metrics['macro_f1']:.4f} | "
                f"val_bal_acc="
                f"{val_metrics['balanced_accuracy']:.4f}"
            )

            # Select the checkpoint using validation macro-F1.
            if val_metrics["macro_f1"] > best_val_f1:
                best_val_f1 = val_metrics["macro_f1"]
                best_epoch = epoch
                epochs_without_improvement = 0

                torch.save(
                    {
                        "model_state_dict": model.state_dict(),
                        "model_name": model_name,
                        "model_key": model_key,
                        "best_epoch": best_epoch,
                        "best_val_macro_f1": best_val_f1,
                        "class_names": CLASS_NAMES,
                    },
                    checkpoint_path,
                )
            else:
                epochs_without_improvement += 1

            if epochs_without_improvement >= PATIENCE:
                print(
                    "Early stopping: validation macro-F1 "
                    "did not improve."
                )
                break

        # Reload the best validation-selected checkpoint.
        checkpoint = torch.load(
            checkpoint_path,
            map_location=DEVICE,
            weights_only=False,
        )
        model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state_dict"])

        best_val_metrics = evaluate_model(
            model, val_loader, criterion
        )

        mlflow.log_metrics({
            "best_epoch": best_epoch,
            "best_val_macro_f1": best_val_f1,
            "best_val_balanced_accuracy":
                best_val_metrics["balanced_accuracy"],
            "best_val_accuracy": best_val_metrics["accuracy"],
            "training_seconds": time.time() - start_time,
        })

        # Save the training history.
        history_path = os.path.join(
            ARTIFACT_DIR,
            f"{model_key}_history.csv",
        )
        pd.DataFrame(history).to_csv(history_path, index=False)
        mlflow.log_artifact(history_path)

        # Save the validation classification report.
        report = classification_report(
            best_val_metrics["y_true"],
            best_val_metrics["y_pred"],
            labels=list(range(NUM_CLASSES)),
            target_names=CLASS_NAMES,
            output_dict=True,
            zero_division=0,
        )

        report_path = os.path.join(
            ARTIFACT_DIR,
            f"{model_key}_validation_report.json",
        )
        with open(report_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(report, f, indent=2)

        mlflow.log_artifact(report_path)

        # Save the validation confusion matrix.
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))

        ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_predictions(
            best_val_metrics["y_true"],
            best_val_metrics["y_pred"],
            labels=list(range(NUM_CLASSES)),
            display_labels=CLASS_NAMES,
            xticks_rotation=30,
            ax=ax,
            colorbar=False,
        )

        fig.tight_layout()

        cm_path = os.path.join(
            ARTIFACT_DIR,
            f"{model_key}_validation_confusion.png",
        )
        fig.savefig(cm_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)

        mlflow.log_artifact(cm_path)
        mlflow.log_artifact(checkpoint_path)

        # Construct the result dictionary before leaving the MLflow run.
        result = {
            "model_key": model_key,
            "model_name": model_name,
            "best_epoch": best_epoch,
            "best_val_macro_f1": best_val_f1,
            "best_val_balanced_accuracy":
                best_val_metrics["balanced_accuracy"],
            "best_val_accuracy": best_val_metrics["accuracy"],
            "trainable_parameters": trainable_count,
            "total_parameters": total_count,
            "training_seconds": time.time() - start_time,
            "run_id": run.info.run_id,
        }

    # Release GPU and data-loader resources.
    del model, train_loader, val_loader
    del train_dataset, val_dataset
    del optimizer, criterion, scaler

    gc.collect()

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # This return is essential: without it, Python returns None.
    return result

5. DINOv2 progression: learning rate and partial fine-tuning¶

After the initial comparison, tune the DINOv2 linear-probe learning rate and then unfreeze a small number of final transformer blocks. Keep the validation Macro-F1 as the checkpoint-selection metric and log every run. Treat small single-run differences as exploratory rather than statistically conclusive.

Initial DINOv2 linear-probe baseline¶

Freeze the pretrained DINOv2 backbone and train a task-specific classifier. This isolates the quality of pretrained representations before testing fine-tuning, head design, loss functions, or augmentation.

In [0]:
def train_linear_probe_tuned(
    model_key,
    model_name,
    learning_rate,
    weight_decay=1e-4,
    max_epochs=15,
    patience=4,
):
    """
    Train a frozen-backbone linear probe with experiment-specific
    hyperparameters, without modifying train_linear_probe().
    """
    seed_everything(SEED)
    start_time = time.time()

    print(
        f"\n{'=' * 65}\n"
        f"Training {model_key} | LR={learning_rate:g} | "
        f"WD={weight_decay:g}\n"
        f"{'=' * 65}"
    )

    train_transform = make_transforms(model_name, training=True)
    eval_transform = make_transforms(model_name, training=False)

    train_dataset = CrisisMMDImageDataset(train_df, train_transform)
    val_dataset = CrisisMMDImageDataset(val_df, eval_transform)

    train_loader = DataLoader(
        train_dataset,
        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
        shuffle=True,
        num_workers=NUM_WORKERS,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
        generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(SEED),
    )
    val_loader = DataLoader(
        val_dataset,
        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
        shuffle=False,
        num_workers=NUM_WORKERS,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
    )

    model = timm.create_model(
        model_name,
        pretrained=True,
        num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    ).to(DEVICE)

    # Freeze the complete backbone and train only the classifier.
    for param in model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = False

    classifier = model.get_classifier()
    if not isinstance(classifier, nn.Module):
        raise TypeError(
            f"Unexpected classifier for {model_name}: "
            f"{type(classifier)}"
        )

    for param in classifier.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True

    trainable_count = sum(
        p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad
    )
    total_count = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())

    counts = (
        train_df["image_damage"]
        .value_counts()
        .reindex(CLASS_NAMES, fill_value=0)
    )

    if (counts == 0).any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Missing training classes: {counts.to_dict()}"
        )

    weights = len(train_df) / (NUM_CLASSES * counts)
    class_weights = torch.tensor(
        weights.values,
        dtype=torch.float32,
        device=DEVICE,
    )

    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=class_weights)

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        filter(lambda p: p.requires_grad, model.parameters()),
        lr=learning_rate,
        weight_decay=weight_decay,
    )

    scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler(
        "cuda",
        enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
    )

    best_val_f1 = -1.0
    best_epoch = 0
    epochs_without_improvement = 0
    history = []

    checkpoint_path = os.path.join(
        ARTIFACT_DIR, f"{model_key}_best.pt"
    )

    try:
        with mlflow.start_run(run_name=f"{model_key}_linear_probe") as run:
            mlflow.log_params({
                "model_key": model_key,
                "model_name": model_name,
                "training_method": "frozen_backbone_linear_probe",
                "seed": SEED,
                "learning_rate": learning_rate,
                "weight_decay": weight_decay,
                "max_epochs": max_epochs,
                "patience": patience,
                "batch_size": BATCH_SIZE,
                "optimizer": "AdamW",
                "loss": "class_weighted_cross_entropy",
                "class_names": json.dumps(CLASS_NAMES),
                "train_rows": len(train_df),
                "validation_rows": len(val_df),
                "trainable_parameters": trainable_count,
                "total_parameters": total_count,
                "device": DEVICE,
            })

            mlflow.log_metrics({
                f"train_class_count_{label}": int(counts[label])
                for label in CLASS_NAMES
            })

            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                # Backbone stays frozen and in evaluation mode.
                model.eval()
                model.get_classifier().train()
                running_loss = 0.0

                for images, labels in train_loader:
                    images = images.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)
                    labels = labels.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)

                    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)

                    with torch.autocast(
                        device_type="cuda",
                        dtype=torch.float16,
                        enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
                    ):
                        logits = model(images)
                        loss = criterion(logits, labels)

                    scaler.scale(loss).backward()
                    scaler.step(optimizer)
                    scaler.update()

                    running_loss += loss.item() * labels.size(0)

                train_loss = running_loss / len(train_dataset)
                val_metrics = evaluate_model(
                    model, val_loader, criterion
                )

                record = {
                    "epoch": epoch,
                    "train_loss": train_loss,
                    "val_loss": val_metrics["loss"],
                    "val_macro_f1": val_metrics["macro_f1"],
                    "val_balanced_accuracy":
                        val_metrics["balanced_accuracy"],
                    "val_accuracy": val_metrics["accuracy"],
                }
                history.append(record)

                mlflow.log_metrics(
                    {
                        k: float(v)
                        for k, v in record.items()
                        if k != "epoch"
                    },
                    step=epoch,
                )

                print(
                    f"Epoch {epoch:02d}/{max_epochs} | "
                    f"train_loss={train_loss:.4f} | "
                    f"val_macro_f1={val_metrics['macro_f1']:.4f} | "
                    f"val_bal_acc="
                    f"{val_metrics['balanced_accuracy']:.4f}"
                )

                if val_metrics["macro_f1"] > best_val_f1:
                    best_val_f1 = val_metrics["macro_f1"]
                    best_epoch = epoch
                    epochs_without_improvement = 0

                    torch.save(
                        {
                            "model_state_dict": model.state_dict(),
                            "model_name": model_name,
                            "model_key": model_key,
                            "best_epoch": best_epoch,
                            "best_val_macro_f1": best_val_f1,
                            "class_names": CLASS_NAMES,
                        },
                        checkpoint_path,
                    )
                else:
                    epochs_without_improvement += 1

                if epochs_without_improvement >= patience:
                    print("Early stopping.")
                    break

            checkpoint = torch.load(
                checkpoint_path,
                map_location=DEVICE,
                weights_only=False,
            )
            model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state_dict"])

            best_val_metrics = evaluate_model(
                model, val_loader, criterion
            )

            mlflow.log_metrics({
                "best_epoch": best_epoch,
                "best_val_macro_f1": best_val_f1,
                "best_val_balanced_accuracy":
                    best_val_metrics["balanced_accuracy"],
                "best_val_accuracy": best_val_metrics["accuracy"],
                "training_seconds": time.time() - start_time,
            })

            history_path = os.path.join(
                ARTIFACT_DIR, f"{model_key}_history.csv"
            )
            pd.DataFrame(history).to_csv(history_path, index=False)
            mlflow.log_artifact(history_path)

            report = classification_report(
                best_val_metrics["y_true"],
                best_val_metrics["y_pred"],
                labels=list(range(NUM_CLASSES)),
                target_names=CLASS_NAMES,
                output_dict=True,
                zero_division=0,
            )

            report_path = os.path.join(
                ARTIFACT_DIR,
                f"{model_key}_validation_report.json",
            )
            with open(report_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
            mlflow.log_artifact(report_path)

            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
            ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_predictions(
                best_val_metrics["y_true"],
                best_val_metrics["y_pred"],
                labels=list(range(NUM_CLASSES)),
                display_labels=CLASS_NAMES,
                xticks_rotation=30,
                ax=ax,
                colorbar=False,
            )
            fig.tight_layout()

            cm_path = os.path.join(
                ARTIFACT_DIR,
                f"{model_key}_validation_confusion.png",
            )
            fig.savefig(cm_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
            plt.close(fig)

            mlflow.log_artifact(cm_path)
            mlflow.log_artifact(checkpoint_path)

            result = {
                "model_key": model_key,
                "model_name": model_name,
                "learning_rate": learning_rate,
                "weight_decay": weight_decay,
                "best_epoch": best_epoch,
                "best_val_macro_f1": best_val_f1,
                "best_val_balanced_accuracy":
                    best_val_metrics["balanced_accuracy"],
                "best_val_accuracy": best_val_metrics["accuracy"],
                "trainable_parameters": trainable_count,
                "total_parameters": total_count,
                "training_seconds": time.time() - start_time,
                "run_id": run.info.run_id,
            }

        return result

    finally:
        del model, train_loader, val_loader
        del train_dataset, val_dataset
        del optimizer, criterion, scaler
        gc.collect()

        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()

Shared imports and runtime checks¶

Imports and runtime checks belong in the setup stage. Later cells should reuse these names rather than re-importing libraries or reinstalling packages.

In [0]:
import os
import gc
import json
import time
import random
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import timm
import mlflow

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from sklearn.metrics import (
    f1_score,
    balanced_accuracy_score,
    accuracy_score,
    classification_report,
    confusion_matrix,
)

def train_dinov2_partial(
    backbone_lr=1e-5,
    head_lr=1e-4,
    weight_decay=1e-4,
    max_epochs=15,
    patience=4,
    seed=42,
    unfreeze_last_n_blocks=1,
):
    model_key = (
        f"DINOv2_partial_b{backbone_lr:g}_h{head_lr:g}"
    )
    started = time.time()

    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)

    model_name = MODEL_CONFIGS["DINOv2_Base"]

    train_dataset = CrisisMMDImageDataset(
        train_df,
        make_transforms(model_name, training=True),
    )
    val_dataset = CrisisMMDImageDataset(
        val_df,
        make_transforms(model_name, training=False),
    )

    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)

    train_loader = DataLoader(
        train_dataset,
        batch_size=16,
        shuffle=True,
        num_workers=2,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
        generator=generator,
    )
    val_loader = DataLoader(
        val_dataset,
        batch_size=16,
        shuffle=False,
        num_workers=2,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
    )

    model = timm.create_model(
        model_name,
        pretrained=True,
        num_classes=NUM_CLASSES,
    ).to(DEVICE)

    # Freeze every parameter first.
    for p in model.parameters():
        p.requires_grad = False

    # Unfreeze the final two transformer blocks.
    for block in model.blocks[-unfreeze_last_n_blocks:]:
        for p in block.parameters():
            p.requires_grad = True

    # Unfreeze final normalization and classification head.
    for p in model.norm.parameters():
        p.requires_grad = True

    for p in model.get_classifier().parameters():
        p.requires_grad = True

    head_ids = {
        id(p) for p in model.get_classifier().parameters()
        if p.requires_grad
    }

    backbone_params = [
        p for p in model.parameters()
        if p.requires_grad and id(p) not in head_ids
    ]
    head_params = [
        p for p in model.get_classifier().parameters()
        if p.requires_grad
    ]

    # Verify parameter groups are disjoint.
    assert not (
        {id(p) for p in backbone_params}
        & {id(p) for p in head_params}
    )

    class_counts = (
        train_df["image_damage"]
        .value_counts()
        .reindex(CLASS_NAMES, fill_value=0)
    )

    if (class_counts == 0).any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Missing training class: {class_counts.to_dict()}"
        )

    weights = len(train_df) / (
        len(CLASS_NAMES) * class_counts
    )
    class_weights = torch.tensor(
        weights.values,
        dtype=torch.float32,
        device=DEVICE,
    )
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=class_weights)

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        [
            {"params": backbone_params, "lr": backbone_lr},
            {"params": head_params, "lr": head_lr},
        ],
        weight_decay=weight_decay,
    )

    scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler(
        "cuda", enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda")
    )

    best_f1 = -1.0
    best_epoch = 0
    stale_epochs = 0
    history = []

    os.makedirs(ARTIFACT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    checkpoint_path = os.path.join(
        ARTIFACT_DIR, f"{model_key}_best.pt"
    )

    with mlflow.start_run(run_name=model_key) as run:
        mlflow.log_params({
            "model_name": model_name,
            "training_method": "partial_finetuning_last_2_blocks",
            "unfrozen_blocks": 2,
            "backbone_lr": backbone_lr,
            "head_lr": head_lr,
            "weight_decay": weight_decay,
            "batch_size": 16,
            "max_epochs": max_epochs,
            "patience": patience,
            "seed": seed,
            "input_size": "518x518",
            "optimizer": "AdamW",
            "loss": "class_weighted_cross_entropy",
            "trainable_parameters": sum(
                p.numel() for p in model.parameters()
                if p.requires_grad
            ),
            "total_parameters": sum(
                p.numel() for p in model.parameters()
            ),
        })

        for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
            # Set all modules to evaluation mode first.
            model.eval()

            # Only train the unfrozen modules.
            for block in model.blocks[-2:]:
                block.train()
            model.norm.train()
            model.get_classifier().train()

            running_loss = 0.0

            for images, labels in train_loader:
                images = images.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)
                labels = labels.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)

                optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)

                with torch.autocast(
                    device_type="cuda",
                    dtype=torch.float16,
                    enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
                ):
                    logits = model(images)
                    loss = criterion(logits, labels)

                scaler.scale(loss).backward()
                scaler.step(optimizer)
                scaler.update()

                running_loss += loss.item() * labels.size(0)

            train_loss = running_loss / len(train_dataset)

            # Evaluate on validation only.
            model.eval()
            y_true, y_pred = [], []
            val_loss_sum = 0.0

            with torch.inference_mode():
                for images, labels in val_loader:
                    images = images.to(
                        DEVICE, non_blocking=True
                    )
                    labels = labels.to(
                        DEVICE, non_blocking=True
                    )

                    with torch.autocast(
                        device_type="cuda",
                        dtype=torch.float16,
                        enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
                    ):
                        logits = model(images)
                        loss = criterion(logits, labels)

                    val_loss_sum += (
                        loss.item() * labels.size(0)
                    )
                    y_true.extend(labels.cpu().tolist())
                    y_pred.extend(
                        logits.argmax(1).cpu().tolist()
                    )

            val_loss = val_loss_sum / len(val_dataset)
            val_f1 = f1_score(
                y_true, y_pred,
                average="macro", zero_division=0
            )
            val_bal_acc = balanced_accuracy_score(
                y_true, y_pred
            )
            val_acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)

            metrics = {
                "train_loss": train_loss,
                "val_loss": val_loss,
                "val_macro_f1": val_f1,
                "val_balanced_accuracy": val_bal_acc,
                "val_accuracy": val_acc,
                "backbone_lr": optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"],
                "head_lr": optimizer.param_groups[1]["lr"],
            }
            mlflow.log_metrics(metrics, step=epoch)
            history.append({"epoch": epoch, **metrics})

            print(
                f"Epoch {epoch:02d}/{max_epochs} | "
                f"train_loss={train_loss:.4f} | "
                f"val_loss={val_loss:.4f} | "
                f"macro_F1={val_f1:.4f} | "
                f"balanced_acc={val_bal_acc:.4f} | "
                f"accuracy={val_acc:.4f}"
            )

            if val_f1 > best_f1:
                best_f1 = val_f1
                best_epoch = epoch
                stale_epochs = 0

                torch.save({
                    "model_state_dict": model.state_dict(),
                    "model_name": model_name,
                    "model_key": model_key,
                    "best_epoch": best_epoch,
                    "best_val_macro_f1": best_f1,
                    "class_names": CLASS_NAMES,
                }, checkpoint_path)
            else:
                stale_epochs += 1

            if stale_epochs >= patience:
                print("Early stopping.")
                break

        # Restore the best validation checkpoint.
        checkpoint = torch.load(
            checkpoint_path,
            map_location=DEVICE,
            weights_only=False,
        )
        model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state_dict"])
        model.eval()

        with torch.inference_mode():
            y_true, y_pred = [], []
            for images, labels in val_loader:
                images = images.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)
                with torch.autocast(
                    device_type="cuda",
                    dtype=torch.float16,
                    enabled=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
                ):
                    logits = model(images)

                y_true.extend(labels.tolist())
                y_pred.extend(logits.argmax(1).cpu().tolist())

        report = classification_report(
            y_true, y_pred,
            labels=list(range(NUM_CLASSES)),
            target_names=CLASS_NAMES,
            output_dict=True,
            zero_division=0,
        )

        report_path = os.path.join(
            ARTIFACT_DIR, f"{model_key}_report.json"
        )
        with open(report_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(report, f, indent=2)

        history_path = os.path.join(
            ARTIFACT_DIR, f"{model_key}_history.csv"
        )
        pd.DataFrame(history).to_csv(
            history_path, index=False
        )

        cm = confusion_matrix(
            y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(NUM_CLASSES))
        )
        cm_path = os.path.join(
            ARTIFACT_DIR, f"{model_key}_confusion.csv"
        )
        pd.DataFrame(
            cm, index=CLASS_NAMES, columns=CLASS_NAMES
        ).to_csv(cm_path)

        mlflow.log_artifact(checkpoint_path)
        mlflow.log_artifact(report_path)
        mlflow.log_artifact(history_path)
        mlflow.log_artifact(cm_path)

        result = {
            "model_key": model_key,
            "best_epoch": best_epoch,
            "best_val_macro_f1": best_f1,
            "best_val_balanced_accuracy": balanced_accuracy_score(
                y_true, y_pred
            ),
            "best_val_accuracy": accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred),
            "trainable_parameters": sum(
                p.numel() for p in model.parameters()
                if p.requires_grad
            ),
            "training_seconds": time.time() - started,
            "run_id": run.info.run_id,
        }

        mlflow.log_metrics({
            "best_epoch": best_epoch,
            "best_val_macro_f1": result["best_val_macro_f1"],
            "best_val_balanced_accuracy":
                result["best_val_balanced_accuracy"],
            "best_val_accuracy": result["best_val_accuracy"],
            "training_seconds": result["training_seconds"],
        })

    del model, optimizer, scaler
    del train_loader, val_loader, train_dataset, val_dataset
    gc.collect()
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    return result

Progressive DINOv2 fine-tuning¶

This experiment unfreezes a limited number of final backbone blocks to adapt pretrained features to disaster imagery. Compare it with the frozen linear probe, while noting that additional trainable parameters increase compute and overfitting risk.

import os
import torch

# 1. Find a checkpoint matching the controlled-model format.
artifact_dir = ARTIFACT_DIR
checkpoint = None
artifact_path = None

for root, _, files in os.walk(artifact_dir):
    for filename in sorted(files):
        if not filename.endswith((".pt", ".pth", ".ckpt")):
            continue

        path = os.path.join(root, filename)

        try:
            candidate = torch.load(
                path,
                map_location="cpu",
                weights_only=False,
            )

            if (
                isinstance(candidate, dict)
                and isinstance(candidate.get("config"), dict)
                and isinstance(candidate.get("state_dict"), dict)
                and "head" in candidate["config"]
                and "blocks" in candidate["config"]
            ):
                checkpoint = candidate
                artifact_path = path
                break

        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"Skipping unreadable checkpoint {path}: {exc}")

    if checkpoint is not None:
        break

# 2. Stop clearly if the expected checkpoint format was not found.
if checkpoint is None:
    print("No compatible controlled-model checkpoint was found.")
    print("Available checkpoint files:")

    for root, _, files in os.walk(artifact_dir):
        for filename in sorted(files):
            if filename.endswith((".pt", ".pth", ".ckpt")):
                print(os.path.join(root, filename))

    print(
        "\nThe available files may belong to the baseline training pipeline. "
        "They cannot automatically be treated as controlled-model checkpoints."
    )

else:
    # 3. Inspect the saved experiment configuration.
    config = checkpoint["config"]

    print("Checkpoint:", artifact_path)
    print("Experiment:", config.get("name", "Not recorded"))
    print("Head:", config["head"])
    print("Unfrozen blocks:", config["blocks"])
    print("Loss:", config.get("loss_name", "Not recorded"))
    print("Gamma:", config.get("gamma", "Not recorded"))
    print("Best epoch:", checkpoint.get("best_epoch", "Not recorded"))

    best_f1 = checkpoint.get("best_val_macro_f1")
    if best_f1 is not None:
        print(f"Best validation Macro-F1: {best_f1:.4f}")

    # 4. Reconstruct the architecture and load exact saved weights.
    device = torch.device(
        "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    )

    model = DINOv2ControlledModel(
        head_type=config["head"],
        unfreeze_blocks=config["blocks"],
    )

    model.load_state_dict(
        checkpoint["state_dict"],
        strict=True,
    )

    model = model.to(device)
    model.eval()

    print("\nCheckpoint loaded successfully.")
    print("Device:", device)

Controlled classifier-head comparison¶

Compare classifier heads while holding the dataset split and backbone strategy constant. The goal is to test whether head capacity or inductive bias improves minority-class recognition, not simply to maximize accuracy.

]

    if p.requires_grad

optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
    [
        {"params": backbone_params, "lr": 1e-5},
        {"params": head_params, "lr": 1e-4},
    ],
    weight_decay=1e-4,
)

6. Controlled DINOv2 architecture and loss experiments¶

Keep the DINOv2 backbone and data split fixed while varying classifier head design and then the loss function. This isolates the effect of head/loss changes more clearly than changing multiple factors at once. Preserve MLflow run metadata and checkpoints for reproducibility.
